title: On Dragging the boat up the whole beach
subtitle: 交通出行 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）
meta: 主题语境：交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）　|　核心词汇：drag　|　正文 350 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 drag 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1960 the guide ① dragged the boat up the whole beach in silence, and every traveller in the valley said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three days on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the guide ② drags the boat up the whole beach twice over without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ drag the boat up the whole beach at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ dragged the boat up the whole beach before — a line in the guidebook for July 1954 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Dragging the boat up the whole beach in silence, the guide said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the map at the far ledge, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ drag the meeting into the night twice over, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Drag the meeting into the night at once and never mention it again.

By 1967 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the guidebook, and a new traveller from the next valley ⑧ drags the meeting into the night in silence every day without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the ledge, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ dragged the boat up the whole beach again when nobody else would.

⑩ To drag the boat up the whole beach, my mother said in 1972, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the valley remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the valley forgets, somebody drags the boat up the whole beach twice over again and somebody must drag the boat up the whole beach in silence all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 拖（一般过去式 dragged the boat up the whole beach：1960 年向导头一回这样做，一言不发地）
B. v. 拖（一般现在 drags the boat up the whole beach：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 拖（不定式 to drag the boat up the whole beach：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 拖（过去完成时 had dragged the boat up the whole beach：1954 年七月的旅行手册上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 拖（动名词 dragging the boat up the whole beach 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 拖长（drag the meeting into the night：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去拖长把会一直拖到夜里）
G. v. 拖长（drag the meeting into the night：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 拖（后段两处：新来的旅人照例 drags the meeting into the night，而母亲又一次 dragged the boat up the whole beach）

answers.why: drag 意为“拖”，1960 年向导一言不发地拖把船拖上整片沙滩，那是山谷里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 dragged。
drag 意为“拖”，自那以后向导来回两遍把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 drags。
drag 意为“拖”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯拖把船拖上整片沙滩”，此处为不定式 to drag the boat up the whole beach。
drag 意为“拖”，旅行手册里 七月 那行字说明早在 1967 年之前就有人拖过，故用过去完成时 had dragged。
drag 意为“拖”，向导说“拖把船拖上整片沙滩这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 dragging the boat up the whole beach 作主语。
drag 意为“拖长”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去拖长把会一直拖到夜里”，should ever 之后用原形 drag the meeting into the night。
drag 意为“拖长”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻拖长把会一直拖到夜里（drag the meeting into the night at once），以后再也不要提起。
drag 意为“拖”，新来的旅人每个日子都照例拖长把会一直拖到夜里，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 drags。
drag 意为“拖”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次一言不发地拖把船拖上整片沙滩，用一般过去式 dragged 叙述。
drag 意为“拖”，结尾那句是母亲 1972 年的话：要拖把船拖上整片沙滩，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和山谷记住的那一件。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1960 年，向导一言不发地拖把船拖上整片沙滩；山谷里每一个旅人都说这是头一回。（dragged the boat up the whole beach）
多年以后，向导仍来回两遍做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（drags the boat up the whole beach）
母亲后来说，难就难在肯拖把船拖上整片沙滩这件事本身。（to drag the boat up the whole beach）
早在 1954 年就有人拖把船拖上整片沙滩，七月那天旅行手册上的一行字就是证据。（had dragged the boat up the whole beach）
向导说过，一言不发地拖把船拖上整片沙滩这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（dragging the boat up the whole beach 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻拖长把会一直拖到夜里，以后再也不要提起。（drag the meeting into the night，祈使句）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 drag 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1960 the guide dragged the boat up the whole beach in silence, and nobody in the valley forgot it.
Even now the guide drags the boat up the whole beach twice over whenever the valley asks.
Dragging the boat up the whole beach in silence, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever drag the meeting into the night twice over, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new traveller from the next valley drags the meeting into the night in silence every day, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother dragged the boat up the whole beach again, and the valley remembered that half.
